title: "Rendering"
description: "Rendering images and animations with the Canvas."
execute:
  daemon: false
---

The [](`~mn.Canvas`) is used to render images and animations of any [](`~mn.Molecule`),
whether it is a single static structure or a multi-frame trajectory. Annotations can be
attached to the molecule and will appear in the render.

```{python}
import molecularnodes as mn
import MDAnalysis as mda
from MDAnalysis.tests.datafiles import PSF, DCD

canvas = mn.Canvas()
```

## Add a Molecule to Blender

```{python}
#| warning: false
u = mda.Universe(PSF, DCD)
mol = mn.Molecule(u).add_style("cartoon")

# add resid 1 and 129 with spheres style, using mesh geometry
mol.add_style("spheres", selection="resid 1 129", sphere_geometry="Mesh")
```

## Add annotations

```{python}
# add universe info annotation
mol.annotations.add_universe_info()

# add COM distance between resid 1 and 129 annotation
mol.annotations.add_com_distance(
    selection1="resid 1", selection2="resid 129", text1="r1", text2="r129"
)
```

## Render an Image

[](`~mn.Canvas.snapshot`) renders a still image and returns it as an
`IPython.display.Image`, which displays automatically when it is the result of a notebook
cell. Pass `path=` to also save the image to disk, `render_scale=` for a quick lower-resolution
preview, and `frame=` to render a specific frame of the scene.

```{python}
# frame the molecule
canvas.look_at(mol)

# render image of scene at frame 75
canvas.snapshot(frame=75)
```

To show a render that isn't the last expression in a cell (e.g. inside a loop), wrap the
call with `display()`:

```python
for frame in [1, 50, 90]:
    display(canvas.snapshot(frame=frame))
```

## Render an Animation

[](`~mn.Canvas.animation`) renders the scene's frame range and returns the result for
display in the notebook — an `IPython.display.Video` for MP4 (the default) or an
`IPython.display.Image` for GIF output (`format="gif"`, which requires the `pillow`
package). As with `snapshot()`, pass `path=` to also save the file to disk; a ``.gif``
suffix on the path selects GIF output automatically. The frame rate can be overridden
per-call with `fps=`.

```{python}
# render animation of scene from frame 10 to 50 at 50% scale
canvas.animation(frame_start=10, frame_end=50, render_scale=50)
```
